author: NorthEast News Desk
body: New Hampshire Superior Court Associate Justice Anne Edwards has been named co-chair of the state's Access to Justice Commission, joining attorney Mark Rouvalis in leading the panel. The commission was created by the New Hampshire Supreme Court to examine unmet civil legal needs, identify barriers to the court system and support initiatives that improve access.

Edwards joined the Superior Court in 2023 after nearly 27 years with the New Hampshire Department of Justice. That background gives the commission a co-chair with experience across state government and the judiciary as it coordinates work among judges, lawyers and organizations that assist people who cannot easily obtain legal representation.

The leadership change comes as the commission continues to assess practical obstacles that can determine whether residents are able to use the civil courts effectively. Those challenges can include the cost of counsel, limited legal information and the complexity of court procedures. Circuit Court Judge Melissa Countway will remain a commission member, preserving continuity as Edwards takes on the co-chair role.
dek: The Superior Court associate justice will help lead the statewide panel that studies civil legal needs and barriers to the courts.
headline: Justice Anne Edwards named co-chair of New Hampshire access commission
